best_for: People who fix computers for family and friends, and IT staff whose company already pays for a TeamViewer license.

points.title: Free only for personal use
points.text: TeamViewer is free for private use. Any work, organizational or paid use needs a commercial license, and only the person giving support needs one, not the device being helped.

points.title: Flags for suspected business use
points.text: If TeamViewer suspects commercial use, connections can fail until you ask for a reset at teamviewer.com/reset and list each ID involved. TeamViewer aims to answer within seven business days, and uninstalling does not clear the flag.

points.title: Yearly subscriptions only
points.text: Paid plans are annual and renew automatically unless you cancel at least 28 days before the term ends. TeamViewer's pricing page did not show list prices in our region at review time, so ask sales for a quote.

points.title: QuickSupport for the other side
points.text: The person receiving help can run QuickSupport, which needs no install and grants temporary access. The full client is for whoever connects in and manages devices.

points.title: Newer Macs only
points.text: TeamViewer lists macOS 14 and later as supported; macOS 13 and older can keep their last compatible version but get no more fixes. On Windows, 7, 8 and 8.1 stop at version 15.64.

points.title: Windows has more history here
points.text: Windows installers come for x86 and x64, plus zip packages including Arm64, all installed for every user. The Windows listing keeps 46 versions; macOS lists only the current universal release.
